hardware.variant: One operator-reported ESP-Mosaico R5 V1.2 kit.

scenario: On one R5 V1.2 device, check the package catalog over HTTP and HTTPS, then run the compiled QML controller through Open, Next, Capture, Use and Ask with both a synthetic test image and a camera frame. The test harness supplies programmatic touches and a loopback Responses fixture.
expected: Catalog downloads have identical bytes. Each worker request contains the active step and a PNG image, the fixture response and thumbnail appear in QML, and Back returns to the same step.
observed: The anonymous catalog GET returned HTTP 200 over both HTTP and HTTPS, 2,156 bytes each, with identical SHA-256 ca9a3620ca49a3b01869a7a43415f099e5746c6be8b37fd2bd6794de80b34e00. HTTPS peer and host verification were enabled with the public ISRG Root X2 certificate. In synthetic-image HIL, programmatic touches drove Open→Next→Capture→Use→Ask; the local fixture received exactly one successful POST (5,437 bytes) containing a synthetic 640×480 PNG (972 bytes) and step 2 context. The expected first response line matched and the thumbnail appeared; Back returned to step 2/3. A second HIL run used a real 640×480 frame from /dev/video0 (SC101IOT), encoded as a 5,626-byte PNG through IEND, and posted it only to the board's loopback fixture. The fixture verified the full step title and instruction; QML showed its explicit test response and thumbnail, and Back returned to step 2/3. The GUI process remained active. These were programmatic touches, not physical user touches.
limits: The package-catalog HTTP/HTTPS check and local Responses-fixture worker check were separate operations.
Both QML HIL runs used programmatic touches. The loopback fixture returned explicit test responses; no live model or external image upload was tested.
The camera frame was used only in the on-device loopback test. Its contents, credentials and private endpoints were not collected in this record.
